title: THIS MUST BE THE ONE.
paragraphs: THIS MUST BE THE ONE.

Tall.
Strong.
Kingly.
The kind of man who makes a room go quiet when he walks in.
The prophet Samuel looked at him and felt it immediately.
This must be the king.
But heaven interrupted.
“No.”
Samuel had come to the house of Jesse in Bethlehem with oil in his hand and a mission from God.

Saul had failed.
A new king would rise.
So Jesse brought out his sons.
First came Eliab.

Broad shoulders.
Warrior posture.
Leadership written across his face.
Samuel thought,
“Surely the Lord’s anointed stands before Him.”
But God answered with a line that still shatters human pride:

“Do not consider his appearance or his height…
The Lord does not look at the things people look at.
People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart.”
— First Samuel 16:7
One by one the brothers passed.

No.
No.
No.
Seven impressive men.
Seven divine refusals.
Until Samuel finally asked Jesse:
“Are these all the sons you have?”
Jesse hesitated.
“Well… there is the youngest.”
Not in the house.
Not in the lineup.
Not even considered.
Out in the fields.
Watching sheep.
His name was David.

A shepherd boy.
Dust on his feet.
Probably smelling like the field.
But when he walked in…
God spoke.

“Arise.
Anoint him.”
Think about that moment.
The prophet almost crowned the wrong man.
Not because Samuel was evil.
Because Samuel was human.

We see height.
God sees humility.

We see charisma.
God sees character.

We see the resume.
God sees the heart beating in secret places.
And here is the deeper Gospel thread.
David, the overlooked shepherd, became king.
But centuries later another Son of David would come.

Not tall.
Not royal-looking.
The prophet Isaiah said of Him:

“He had no beauty or majesty to attract us to Him.”
— Book of Isaiah 53:2
That Son of David is Jesus Christ.

Rejected by human eyes.
Chosen by God.
The King we almost would have missed.
Friend, hear this carefully.
God is not searching for the most impressive person in the room.
He is searching for the heart that belongs to Him.

The heart that repents.
The heart that trusts Christ.
The heart that says,
“Lord, I am Yours.”
And when Jesus saves a heart like that—
He turns shepherds into kings.
If this stirred something in you, pause and pray:

“Lord Jesus, look into my heart.
Remove what is false.
Create in me a heart that is fully Yours.”
Because the God who rejected Eliab…
is the same God who lifted David.
And the same Savior who died and rose again is still rewriting stories today.
